raw_findings.message: The displayed tax is calculated on the subtotal instead of the discounted net, so invoices with a discount show tax that disagrees with the computed total.
The user-controlled `--out` path is concatenated into a shell command, so shell metacharacters in the path can execute arbitrary commands.
The price check accepts positive infinity, which `JSON.parse` can produce from an overflowing numeric literal, leading to infinite totals or `null` values in JSON output.
Malformed item entries are silently skipped, so a partially invalid input file produces an invoice that omits items rather than rejecting the input.
When the net amount is zero, this division returns `NaN` or infinity, causing the printed effective tax rate to be invalid.
On a partial final page, this index is beyond the item array, so invoices with more than one page and a non-multiple-of-`perPage` item count throw when accessing `last.sku`.

fixed_raw_findings.message: The supplied date is never checked against the documented YYYY-MM-DD format, so arbitrary strings are accepted and used in both the displayed invoice and its ID.

Customer, date, SKU, and description values are interpolated into plain-text output without escaping control characters, so crafted input can inject terminal escape sequences or forged invoice lines when the output is displayed.
This check accepts Infinity because it only tests the type and whether the value is negative; a JSON price such as `1e400` then produces non-finite invoice totals instead of being rejected.
`Number.isInteger` accepts integers beyond JavaScript's safe-integer range, so a sufficiently large quantity loses precision or overflows during subtotal calculations and yields incorrect totals.
A finite but extremely large tax rate is accepted and can overflow this multiplication; for example, `--tax 1e308` makes tax and total Infinity on an ordinary invoice.

raw_findings.message: Customer names and item text are inserted into the invoice without escaping, so input containing newlines can forge or obscure invoice fields in the rendered document.
The displayed tax is calculated from the subtotal rather than the discounted net amount, so invoices with a discount show a tax figure inconsistent with the total.
The user-controlled output path is concatenated into a shell command, so a path containing shell metacharacters can execute arbitrary commands.
The unit-price check accepts Infinity, which can be supplied as a JSON number such as 1e400 and then produces non-finite invoice totals.
Negative integer quantities are accepted, allowing input to create negative line totals and reduce or reverse the invoice subtotal.
Invalid items are caught and silently discarded, so a malformed item can be omitted from the invoice without alerting the user.
Discounts are checked only for finiteness, so negative discounts or discounts above 100% are accepted and can produce surcharges or negative invoice totals.
When the net amount is zero, this calculation returns NaN or Infinity, which is then printed as the effective tax rate for a zero-value invoice.
For a final page containing fewer than perPage items, this index is out of bounds and reading last.sku throws, so invoices with more than one page and a partial final page fail.

fixed_raw_findings.message: Customer, date, invoice ID, and item text are written raw into the text invoice, so embedded newlines or terminal escape sequences can forge invoice content or manipulate a terminal.
This check accepts Infinity because it only rejects values below zero, so a JSON price such as 1e400 can make invoice totals NaN or Infinity.
Number.isInteger accepts integers beyond JavaScript's safe-integer range, so a large quantity can silently lose precision in line totals and invoice totals.
Multiplying decimal prices by 100 can produce binary floating-point values just below a half-cent, so a price such as 1.005 is rounded to 1.00 instead of 1.01.
A sufficiently large finite tax rate can overflow this multiplication and produce an infinite tax amount; for example, the CLI accepts --tax 1e308.

fixed_raw_findings.message: The supplied date is never validated, so values that are not YYYY-MM-DD dates are emitted on invoices and inserted into invoice IDs, breaking the documented date format and sortable date prefix.

Untrusted customer, date, SKU, and description values are written into the text invoice without escaping control characters or newlines, allowing an input to spoof invoice fields or inject terminal escape sequences.

Prices and quantities are not bounded to values whose cent conversions and products remain finite and safely representable, so accepted inputs such as a very large price or quantity can produce incorrect totals or NaN/Infinity output.
